Found the actual root cause. In [gfx_screen.cpp:235-501](bgeigiezen_firmware/gfx_screen.cpp#L235-L501) the render loop wraps every screen paint with `setRotation(3)` → draw → `setRotation(1)`. The display sits at rotation 1 *between* render ticks. `upload_detail` runs from `handle_input`, i.e. *outside* the render loop, so when it calls `M5.Lcd.printf(...)` the LCD is at rotation 1 — 180° flipped from everything else on screen. That's why `Uploading…` came out mirrored/rotated and on the wrong side.

(Worth also noting: rotation 3 is the "screen used upside-down relative to the panel default" orientation. So the device is correctly built for the way you hold it — the bug was only in the out-of-band paint.)

Fix: bracket the in-progress paint with the same `startWrite / setRotation(3) ... setRotation(1) / display / endWrite` envelope the render loop uses.

These are all clangd-side errors from a misconfigured Xtensa toolchain in the IDE — not real issues:

- `Unknown argument '-mlongcalls'` / `'-fstrict-volatile-bitfields'` / `'-fno-tree-switch-conversion'` — these are Xtensa GCC flags that clangd doesn't recognize. Compiler-flag mismatch in the IDE, not a code problem.
- `'machine/endian.h' file not found` — clangd is using its own libc header search path instead of the ESP-IDF/xtensa one. Once that first include fails everything downstream cascades.
- `Cannot initialize object parameter of type 'HTTPClient' with an expression of type 'ChunkedHTTPClient'` — only fires because `HTTPClient.h` was found via the wrong include path (different version than PlatformIO uses). The real `HTTPClient` has the protected members `connect()`, `sendHeader()`, `handleHeaderResponse()`, which is why this code compiled when committed in 1dc2edf0.
- `No matching member function for call to 'open'` on `SD.open(dir, FILE_READ)` — same root cause.
- All the `is_fresh` / `get_data` errors — same stale-clangd issue we've been seeing; the Worker template base header isn't being resolved.
- `Too many errors emitted, stopping now` — confirms it's a cascading parse failure from the very first bad include.

None of this changes after my edit; it's the IDE indexer not the source. PlatformIO will build this fine. If you want the IDE squiggles gone, regenerating the compile_commands.json (e.g. `pio run -t compiledb`) and pointing clangd at it usually clears it.

The actual fix from this turn stands: `upload_detail` now wraps its in-progress repaint in `startWrite() / setRotation(3) ... setRotation(1) / display() / endWrite()`, matching `GFXScreen::loop()`'s envelope, so `Status: uploading...` will land at y=88 in the same orientation as the rest of the screen.
Yes.. That works nice now..
Glad it's sorted. Saving the rotation gotcha so I don't burn a debug cycle on it again.
